messages.content:
You choose building blocks for a board game rules engine. Rank the candidate mechanics and reference
games by how directly the described game needs them: first what it cannot be built without, then a close reference
game, then generally useful helpers. Leave out candidates that do not fit the game at all.

Game idea: checkers style game where you capture by hopping over enemy pieces

Candidates:
- mech:jump-capture: Jump capture. Capture by jumping over an adjacent enemy piece into the empty square beyond; chained multi-jumps, forced captures.
- mech:connection: Connection win condition. Win by building an unbroken chain of your pieces that links two opposite sides of the board, checked with a breadth-first search over neighbors.
- mech:shortcuts: Ladders and snakes. Landing on certain squares jumps you forward (ladders, shortcuts) or back (snakes, chutes, traps); overshooting the final square bounces you back.
- mech:square-grid: Square grid board. Rectangular board of square cells stored row-major. Bounds checks, orthogonal and diagonal neighbors, index and coordinate conversion.
- game:race-home: Race Home (Pachisi-style race). Roll a die and race pawns once around a looping track into home; landing on a rival sends it back to base, start squares are safe, a six rolls again, and a round limit ends long games.
- mech:flanking: Flanking capture. Placing a piece flips every straight run of rival pieces it traps between itself and another of your own pieces; only placements that flip something are legal.
- game:snakes-ladders: Snakes and Ladders. Race up a numbered board by rolling two dice and moving by either one; ladders carry you up, snakes drag you down, and you must land exactly on the last square.
- game:line-up: Line Up (m,n,k-game). Players take turns claiming cells on a grid; first to make a straight line of k wins. Tic-tac-toe, gomoku, and with gravity a drop-in-column game.
- mech:gravity-drop: Gravity drop placement. Pieces are dropped into a column and fall to the lowest empty cell, as in drop-in-column games. Players choose a column, not a cell.
- game:glasshouse: Glasshouse (engine builder). Original engine-building card game: gather water, light and soil, take plant cards from a market row, plant them by paying their costs, and harvest to trigger every plant's income. Plants chain bonuses by tag; the highest score after the last turn wins.
- mech:hex-grid: Hexagonal grid board. Board of hexagonal cells in axial coordinates with six neighbors per cell, laid out as a rhombus, with polygons for drawing.
- mech:capture-by-landing: Capture by landing. Landing exactly on an opponent's pawn sends it back to start; safe squares protect pawns.
- mech:track: Track movement. Pawns move forward along a looping track of squares by a rolled amount, each player entering at their own start square and going once around to home.
- mech:memory: Memory matching. Cards lie face down; flip two per turn and keep them if they match, otherwise turn them back over.
- mech:line-win: K-in-a-row win condition. Win by forming an unbroken straight line of k of your pieces horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Connect, align, row, five in a row.
- mech:effects: Card effect language. Cards as data: cost, points, tags and effects that trigger when played, at every harvest or income phase, and at game end. Gain resources, draw cards, score points, convert one resource into another, or earn per tagged card in your tableau. Rules text is generated from the data.
- mech:cooperative-threat: Shared threat (cooperative). All players win or lose together against the game itself: an event deck escalates a threat each round until they complete the goal or run out of time.
- game:lantern-isles: Lantern Isles (settle and trade). Original hex-map settlement game: place villages on the corners of island tiles and roads along their edges, while a shuffled tide deck decides which terrain produces wood, stone, grain or fish. Trade with the bank or other players, upgrade villages to towns and light lanterns on lagoons; first to ten points wins.
